solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Foundation has to beg and so on in financially hopeless state

indicators.note: the begging and the 'and so on' sit in the middle of the foundation word

parts.note: a foundation is a base
to beg is to ask

explanation.surface: A charitable foundation reduced to begging is in a hopeless financial state.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something that is a hopeless wreck, especially financially ruined, is informally called this.

clue.text: Heating surface set up right for quantum physicist

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word for the heating surface is written upwards

parts.note: a hob is the heating surface on top of a cooker

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a hotplate correctly for a physicist to use.
explanation.definitionFit: Niels Bohr, the Danish physicist, was a founder of quantum theory and the model of the atom.

clue.text: A tot and Batman ultimately entrapped by Riddler

indicators.note: the last letter of Batman is held inside the riddler word

parts.note: a riddle is a coarse sieve, so a riddler is one that sifts

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of Batman

explanation.surface: Batman ends up caught by his enemy the Riddler, a comic-book villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddler' reads as the Batman villain, but here it is one who riddles, that is sieves.
explanation.definitionFit: A small measure of spirits, a tot, is informally a snifter.

clue.text: Comedy about classes, each retaining old money by way of toughness

indicators.note: the abbreviation for each holds on to the other pieces between its two letters

parts.note: a ducat was an old gold coin
in can mean by way of, as in paying in cash
grit is toughness of character

explanation.surface: A comedy about social classes, with everyone hanging on to old money through sheer toughness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classes' is a double pun: the Willy Russell play is about a working-class woman taking Open University classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Willy Russell's comic play (and film) follows a hairdresser's education and her crossing of class lines.

clue.text: Acts theatrically, skipping up English pitching area

indicators.note: skipping means the word up is left out of the phrase for acting theatrically

parts.note: to camp it up is to act in an exaggerated theatrical way
the word up given as it is

explanation.surface: An actor overacts, skipping ahead of an English player on a cricket pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A site where tents are pitched is a camping ground, so it is a pitching area.

clue.text: Besides doffing cap, one dressed stylishly

indicators.note: doffing a cap is taking off the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: besides means as well, in addition

explanation.surface: Besides taking his hat off, a man is smartly dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell is old slang for a fashionable, smartly dressed person of style.

clue.text: Goethe's first person to encapsulate time and desire

indicators.note: the German pronoun wraps round the letter for time

parts.note: Goethe wrote in German, where the first person singular pronoun is ich

explanation.surface: Goethe's narrator captures the passing of time and longing, a Romantic theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goethe's' signals German, so the first person pronoun is ICH rather than I.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving or longing for something.

clue.text: Rising number consists of deterioration in strain

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the whole run of pieces is written upwards

parts.note: consists of is equivalent to is, as in the team is eleven players
rot is decay or deterioration

explanation.surface: A growing figure is made of the rot inside a stressed structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns the whole phrase NO IS ROT backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsion is the twisting stress or strain on an object turned at one end.

clue.text: Person having mother carefully observe German one in clinch

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the word for a clinch

parts.note: a clinch is an embrace, a hug
ma is mother
NB, nota bene, means note well
ein is German for one

explanation.surface: Someone, watched closely by their mother, catches a German in an embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Any person is a member of the species, a mortal individual of humankind.

clue.text: Elated murmur, if you're listening to it, here's an example

indicators.note: listening means the phrase for an elated murmur is heard, not read

parts.note: elated is high and a murmur is a coo, giving high coo

explanation.surface: A happy murmur, and if you listen closely, here is an example of the form.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue itself scans five, seven, five syllables, so it is the example it points to.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue is a three-line Japanese poem of five, seven and five syllables, so it is a specimen of the form.

clue.text: Eddy Merckx, initially behind noted leader, overtaking cyclist in the middle

indicators.note: the first letter of Merckx comes after the rest
the conductor word takes in the middle letter of cyclist

parts.note: a maestro is a conductor, the leader of musicians playing notes

indicators.note: the middle letter of the seven-letter word cyclist
initially means the first letter of Merckx

explanation.surface: Eddy Merckx, the Belgian champion cyclist, starts behind the leader but overtakes in the middle of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eddy' is Merckx's first name in the surface but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, an eddy of water on a large scale.

clue.text: Insult result of eating pancake (instead of wearing it)?

definitions.text: result of eating pancake (instead of wearing it)?
definitions.meaning: pancake is make-up, called slap; wearing it puts slap on the face, eating it puts it inside

explanation.surface: An insult arises when someone eats the pancake rather than ending up with it on their face.
explanation.walkthrough: Slap is British theatrical slang for make-up, and pancake is a heavy foundation make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuff or affront is figuratively a blow across the cheek.

clue.text: Farcical travails with nanny like a notorious bloodsucker

indicators.note: farcical suggests chaos, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A nanny's ridiculous troubles make her seem like a vampire to the children.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Dracula, the famous vampire, came from the Romanian region of Transylvania.

clue.text: Stelios finally pushes own plane

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of Stelios

parts.note: to poke is to push or prod
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Stelios, founder of easyJet, finally promotes his own aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests Stelios's airline, but it is the woodworker's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A spokeshave is a small two-handled plane for shaping curved wood such as wheel spokes.

clue.text: Beset by pains, problem for manual workers goes on

indicators.note: the injury letters are surrounded by the word for pains

parts.note: pains, as in nuisances, are pests
RSI, repetitive strain injury, troubles people working with their hands

explanation.surface: Surrounded by aches, a hand-workers' ailment continues.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to continue or carry on steadily.

clue.text: Intended expelling first pair for insubordination

indicators.note: the first two letters of the word for insubordination are thrown out

parts.note: defiance is open insubordination

explanation.surface: A trainee intended for promotion is expelled for insubordination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intended' reads as a verb but is the noun, a betrothed man.
explanation.definitionFit: One's intended is the man one is engaged to marry.

clue.text: Crook is for the third time to switch second home designation over?

indicators.note: over means the whole phrase is turned backwards

parts.note: re means again, a second time; two of them make a third time
flipping was the 2009 MPs' expenses practice of switching which home was designated the second one

explanation.surface: Is the crook flipping his second home for the third time?
explanation.walkthrough: In the 2009 British MPs' expenses scandal, flipping meant redesignating one's second home to claim more expenses.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilferer is a petty thief, a crook who steals small things.

clue.text: Unreliable patch results when arbitrator's lead is replaced by two successors

indicators.text: lead is replaced by two successors
indicators.note: the first letter of the arbitrator word gives way to the two letters that follow it in the alphabet

parts.note: a judge arbitrates between parties

explanation.surface: A shaky compromise results when the referee's leading role passes to two followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A kludge is a clumsy, makeshift fix in computing or engineering, liable to fail.

clue.text: Incompetent former Yugoslav racketeer entering America

indicators.note: the tennis player's name goes inside the abbreviation for America

parts.note: US is America
Monica Seles, the tennis player, was born in the former Yugoslavia

explanation.surface: An inept gangster from the former Yugoslavia comes into the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racketeer' suggests a gangster; here it is one who wields a tennis racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone useless at a task is incompetent at it.

clue.text: Hobnail boot's tip damaged in cross-country event

indicators.note: damaged means the letters are knocked out of their order
the tip of the boot is its first letter

explanation.surface: A hobnail boot's toe gets damaged during a cross-country run.
explanation.definitionFit: The biathlon combines cross-country skiing with rifle shooting.

clue.text: Girl due to lose weight, caught with a line

parts.note: a lass is a girl

indicators.note: to lose means the weight letter is dropped from the word for due

parts.note: owed means due

explanation.surface: A girl due to slim down is caught by a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a looped rope, so an animal so caught has been roped with a line.

clue.text: They're gone in fantastic sale prices

parts.note: fantastic, in the sense of excellent, is special
those who go off are offers, people who have gone

explanation.surface: Bargains vanish in a brilliant sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They're gone' is read whimsically as off-ers, people who are off.
explanation.definitionFit: Discounted prices in a sale are promotions, reduced deals.

clue.text: Dive in Hollywood could be packed

parts.note: Hollywood is in LA, Los Angeles
a dive is a seedy bar, a den

explanation.surface: A seedy Hollywood dive could be crowded.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded or heavily burdened, as a packed bag is.

clue.text: Crowd full of upper members?

definitions.meaning: a large number of people, a host
jokingly, having lots of arms, the upper limbs

explanation.surface: A crowd full of upper-class members.
explanation.definitionFit: A large crowd or host is figuratively a whole legion of people.

clue.text: Exodus accepted by a settler who created an ancient empire

indicators.note: the abbreviation for the book is taken in by the settler phrase

parts.note: a lander is one who lands, a settler arriving in new territory
Ex is the abbreviation for the Bible book of Exodus

explanation.surface: A mass departure is welcomed by a pioneer who founded an empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great built a vast empire stretching from Greece to India.

clue.text: Travellers touring university recalled intrigue

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards
the travellers go round the university letter

parts.note: the Roma are a travelling people

explanation.surface: Travellers on a university tour remembered some scheming.
explanation.definitionFit: An intrigue can be a secret love affair, which is what an amour is.

clue.text: Natural drug blotting out time in Illinois, etc

indicators.note: blotting out means the time-zone letters are erased from the drug

parts.note: ecstasy is a drug
CST, Central Standard Time, is the time zone of Illinois and other central US states

explanation.surface: A natural drug free of time restrictions in Illinois and elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drug' suggests just E; the whole drug name is needed, less the time-zone letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy, as in an easy manner, means relaxed and unforced, so natural.

clue.text: Frosty field with runny liquid

indicators.note: liquid means the letters flow into a new shape

explanation.surface: A frozen field with running liquid on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runny' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'liquid' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A frosty reception is cold and hostile, so the manner is cold.
